questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

He who laughs last laughs loudest

options.text: Success in early life ensures success later also
He who laughs last has more energy
The person who understands the joke late laughs loudest
He who focuses on winning in the long term is successful

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'He who focuses on winning in the long term is successful'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Let's see the detailed meaning of the given idiom **'He who laughs last, laughs loudest'**:

 
• The person who has the final, decisive move or victory in a feud, quarrel, or competition is the only one who is truly successful.

Now, let's understand it through an **example:**

 
• Rohit waited years for revenge for what his colleague did to him, but as they say **he who laughs last, laughs loudest.**

questions.question:
The statement below has been given with bracketed text, Select the option with correct Idiom for the bracketed text.

Mom said these instructions are (not understood by her) and that we should show them to Dad.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Greek to her**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The correct idiom to replace the bracketed text is mentioned in option 1.**
 
• The idiom 'Greek to someone' means that something is not understandable to them.' (कुछ उनकी समझ में नहीं आ रहा है)
 
 
• Example: He tried to explain the rules of the game to me, but it was all Greek to me.
 
 
 
• The use of 'her' in the sentence indicates that the speaker is referring to their mother.
 
• **The sentence implies that the mother is having difficulty understanding the instructions.**

Hence, **the correct answer is option 1**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 2 (smart cookie to her) means that someone is intelligent or clever, but it does not fit in the context of the sentence.

 
 
• ​कोई बुद्धिमान या चतुर है
 
 
 
• Option 3 (pound the investment to her) is not an idiom and does not make sense in the sentence.
 
• Option 4 (full of beans to her) means that someone is energetic or enthusiastic, but it does not fit in the context of the sentence.
 
 
• कोई ऊर्जावान या उत्साही है

questions.question:
**Direction: In the following question, out of the given four alternatives, select the alternative which best expresses the meaning of the meaning of the idiom/Phrase.**

Rolling in cash

options.text: Have a large quantity of money

questions.solution:
Here, the correct answer is **"Have a large quantity of money."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **"Rolling in cash"** is an idiomatic expression that means someone has a large amount of money or is very wealthy. (किसी के पास बड़ी मात्रा में धन है या वह बहुत अमीर है)
 
• The phrase suggests a person is figuratively rolling or swimming in a substantial amount of cash, indicating financial abundance or prosperity.
 
• It's a colloquial way of describing someone who is very well-off or financially successful.
 
 
• **Example**: *Despite the economic downturn, the successful entrepreneur found himself **rolling in cash**__ due to wise investments.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. **

Your guess is as good as mine

options.text: To have the same idea as another
To have no idea of the answer
To have a better idea than others

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'To have no idea of the answer'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate answer for the given idiom** 'Your guess is as good as mine' **is** 'To have no idea of the answer'.**
 
• **Your guess is as good as mine:** used for emphasis when one doesn't know the answer to a question. (जोर देने के लिए उपयोग किया जाता है जब किसी को किसी प्रश्न का उत्तर नहीं पता होता है)
 
 
• *Example: "What's her problem?" "I have no idea. **Your guess is as good as mine**."*

 
 
 

**Correct Answer:__** *To have no idea of the answer*.
